list: The official 55 trophies, 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze
note: Names, descriptions and grades are as PlayStation publishes them. Guides are written for this entry, in our own words, from the official descriptions. Where a place or step is not pinned down, the guide says so plainly.

sources.covers: official trophy names, descriptions and grades
sources.name: Exophase

sources.covers: grades and the counts PlayStation tracks
sources.name: PSNProfiles

trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing to do for this one directly. Work through the roadmap in this guide in order — story first, then stranger strands, collectibles, activities, and finally the cleanup trophies — and this one unlocks itself at the end. If your tracker shows 54 of 55, check the one left over rather than replaying the story.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, from start to finish. It is the first story mission, so this is normally the first trophy most players earn. Follow the on-screen objectives; there is no special requirement beyond completing the mission, and story missions can be replayed, so nothing here can be missed.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. The trophy pops when the chapter's final mission ends and the chapter closes. Play the missions in the order the game offers them; if you get stuck on one, replay it from the mission menu — chapter trophies only need the missions completed, not a particular rating.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. The name is printed here exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included. Like the other chapter trophies, it only asks that the chapter be completed, so keep pushing the story forward and it will come on its own.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. By this point the story opens up across Leonida, so it is worth clearing side content as it appears rather than leaving it all for the end — but the chapter trophy itself only needs the story missions done.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, so once it pops you are one final mission away from the story's end. Keep a save from before the final stretch in case you want to mop up anything else first.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Play and complete the final story mission. It is one of only two gold trophies, and it marks the end of the main story. Finish the mission and the gold pops. Before starting it, consider clearing any side trophies you want done first, since the post-story world is usually the cleanup phase — the roadmap in this guide puts cleanup after the story for exactly that reason.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Mission-named trophies like this one unlock on completion alone — no time limit, no special approach, no score to beat. If you fail a section, the mission restarts from a checkpoint and you can try again.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions tend to have a setup phase followed by the job itself; follow the objectives in order and the trophy pops when the mission ends. Nothing in the description asks for a stealthy or fast run, so play it however suits you.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Like the other mission trophies, completion is the whole requirement. The title hints at a family thread in the story, but the trophy itself asks for nothing beyond finishing the mission.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Finish the mission and the trophy is yours. If the mission has a performance or chase section, take it steady — failing and retrying from a checkpoint does not cost you the trophy.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. The name suggests taking something — or someone — down at the airport, but the trophy only requires finishing the mission. Expect a combat-heavy stretch and use cover and the game's combat focus when the fighting starts.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation-style name points to a larger set-piece mission; work through its objectives in order and the trophy pops at the end. As with every story mission, replaying is available if you fail partway through.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion on the in-game stats screen. This is the second gold trophy and the real long haul of the platinum: it counts story missions, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and the rest of the checklist the game itself tracks. Use this guide's tracker alongside the in-game completion percentage — when a category is finished here, check it off there. Leave this for the final cleanup stage; chasing it early burns time on content you would meet naturally later.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, airtime and the like — while driving around Leonida. The count is cumulative across the whole game, so every stunt you land while travelling counts toward it. The fastest honest way is to keep driving fast and jumping ramps and hills as you move between objectives instead of fast-travelling everywhere; the number climbs on its own over a full playthrough, and the post-story cleanup is a good time to grind out whatever is left.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try all 9 activity types at least once — the game counts distinct types, not repeats, so one go at each is enough. Work through whatever activities the map offers (racing, shooting range, fishing, bowling, arcade and the rest) and tick them off as you try them. This is a good early trophy: sampling everything once also shows you which activities you enjoy enough to grind for their own trophies later.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is a skill trophy, not a grind: each challenge has a gold score to beat, and you can retry any challenge as many times as you like, so nothing is missable. Learn the range's scoring — accuracy and speed both matter — practise the weapon types you are weakest with, and take the challenges in short sessions rather than all at once. Gold on all 42 is the second-hardest shooting ask in the list, after the stunt and collectible grinds.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. You need a win at every location, not just 14 wins anywhere, so keep a note of which locations you have already won at. Drone racing is about smooth lines and cutting corners without crashing; learn one location's course before moving on, and return to any location you lost at — races can be retried freely.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — distinct events, so winning the same race twice only counts once. Spread your wins across the race types the game offers and keep track of which you have already won. Pick the vehicle class you drive best, learn the course on a practice run if one is offered, and do not be afraid to retry: a loss costs nothing but time.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are head-to-head, so this is about out-fishing one rival rather than hitting a score. Learn the fishing timing — hook, reel and line tension — in a practice session first, then take the challenge when you are comfortable. The challenge can be retried, so a loss is just a lesson.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game from start to end. Find an arcade machine, pick a game, and play it through to its conclusion — reaching the end screen is what counts, not a high score. If the first game you try is too hard, try a different machine; any completed arcade game earns the trophy.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand through to its final mission. Stranger and side-character strands unlock as the story progresses, so meet Andy when his missions appear and keep returning when new ones open up. The trophy pops when his last mission ends. Strands are part of the 100% completion picture, so clearing them in the story's second stage keeps the endgame short.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's mission strand through to its final mission. Like the other named-character strands, his missions appear over the course of the story — do them when they show up rather than letting them pile up. The trophy pops on the final mission's completion.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand through to its final mission. Billy's strand is one of several that feed the Strangers & Freaks silver, so clearing it also moves that bigger trophy forward. Keep an eye out for his missions between story chapters.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida. This is the silver that ties the side content together: each named stranger — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and the others — has a strand, and finishing one counts toward the 8. Do stranger missions as they appear during and after the story, and check the tracker to see which strands you have finished. It pairs naturally with the individual strand trophies, so you will likely earn several of those on the way to this one.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's mission strand through to its final mission. Randy's missions are part of the stranger strands, so they count toward the Strangers & Freaks silver too. Play his strand when it appears and finish it before moving on to the next chapter if you can.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand through to its final mission. Tyrone is another of the stranger characters whose strand feeds the 8-strand silver. Clear his missions as they unlock and the bronze pops with his finale.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. These are quiet, scenic places — expect viewpoints, beaches and high ground — and the game tracks how many you have used, so work through them as you explore rather than hunting them all at once. Pair this with exploring Leonida's 52 areas: every new area you visit is a chance to find a spot you have not meditated at yet. No location is pinned down here, because none was verified in-game for this guide.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. This is a stranger-strand hunt: follow Bret's strand until the hunt is offered, then track the animal and take it down. Hunting calls for patience — move quietly, watch the animal's behaviour, and take a clean shot. The trophy is about that one unique animal, not general hunting, so follow Bret's thread specifically.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets. Cards are scattered across Leonida, and a set is only complete when every card in it is found — the game's counter tracks your progress, so check it as you go. Collect cards whenever you pass through a new area instead of saving them all for the end, and keep this trophy in the collectibles stage of the roadmap alongside the WAiNK locations and the meditation spots.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK feature at 100 different locations. This is the biggest location grind in the list, so treat it as a travelling companion to everything else: WAiNK at every new place you visit, and the count climbs without a dedicated grind. The game's tracker shows how many locations you have covered, so you can see how many are left before the final push. Save the last few for the cleanup stage, when you can sweep the remaining areas deliberately.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges of any kind. Challenges are the game's small objectives scattered through activities and exploration, and they add up across everything you do — races, shooting, stunts and more. You will clear a good chunk of the 50 naturally on the way to the other trophies; the rest is a matter of opening the challenge list, picking the ones closest to done, and finishing them off in the cleanup stage.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose the police and escape. The wording implies a shared escape — a partner moment, not a solo one — so make sure your partner is with you before you start raising heat. Raise the wanted level, then break line of sight, get out of the search area and stay hidden until the stars clear. Treat this as a one-off set-piece: plan it, save first, and retry if the escape fails.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without losing your wanted level between them. The trick is in the phrase 'without losing' — you need to keep the heat alive across all three robberies, so move fast from shop to shop and do not let the police lose you in between. Plan a route with three shops close together, save first, and keep your partner with you for all three. If the wanted level drops, the chain breaks and you start over.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. The game counts a vehicle as discovered when you first encounter or drive it, so variety is the goal — try every car, bike, boat and aircraft you come across instead of sticking to one favourite. Visiting different areas and vehicle spots helps, and this pairs well with exploring all 52 areas of Leonida and with the Scooter Bros registrations.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. This is about picking the right fight: find a spot with at least 5 enemies grouped together, trigger Combat Focus, and chain the takedowns before it ends. A busy mission firefight or a wanted-level standoff is the natural place to try it. If you only manage 3 or 4, the count resets — you need all 5 inside one activation, so set the fight up first and then commit.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from Vice City International Airport — in plain terms, leave the airport in a way the schedule never planned, by taking an aircraft out yourself. Head to VCIA, get hold of a plane, and take off. The description reads like a one-off moment rather than a repeatable activity, so plan it deliberately and save first; no specific aircraft or runway is named here, because none was verified in-game for this guide.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The description is a joke about Rhinos — the tanks — and the trophy is about dealing with them. Expect a moment involving a Rhino tank, most likely in a mission or a high-wanted-level rampage, where you take one on or take one over. No exact step is claimed here, because the official description does not spell one out; when a Rhino shows up in your game, engage it and see what the moment asks of you.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get out without ever being detected. Stealth is the whole requirement: go in quietly, avoid cameras and staff sightlines, take what you came for and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — leave, reset and try again, ideally with a save from just before you walk in. Plan the approach before you start, and do not rush the exit.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault is its own job: get in, crack the vault, and get clear of the police afterwards. The count is cumulative, so you can do the five across the whole game — but plan each escape route before you start, because the getaway is where these jobs are won or lost. This is the silver robbery trophy, and it pairs naturally with the armored-truck robbery.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape afterwards. Armored trucks appear on the roads of Leonida; intercept one, stop it, take the cash, and then lose the police. The robbery itself is the easy half — the escape is the part to plan, so pick a truck in an area with good getaway routes and keep a fast vehicle nearby.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. The game tracks which areas you have visited, so this is a map-completion trophy: drive, fly and sail into every corner of the state, including the outlying countryside and islands, not just Vice City. It pairs with the meditation spots, the WAiNK locations and discovering 100 vehicles — explore thoroughly once, and several trophies move at the same time.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. That means nine different gangs, one operation each — hitting the same gang twice does not count twice. Keep a list of which gangs you have already hit, and work through the operations as they appear on the map. Expect each gang's turf to fight back, so go in prepared.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a quiet, one-off moment trophy: go to Ocean Beach, find a spot to order or enjoy a cocktail with the view, and take it in. It reads like a single specific moment rather than a repeatable activity, so do it when you are in the area and do not assume it will come up again on its own. No exact bar or spot is named here, because none was verified in-game for this guide.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom, in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass and out the other side. Pick a vehicle showroom, get a car inside or drive one in, and then power out through the front. It is a one-off stunt moment, so save first, line the car up, and go for it.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — and follow through, which suggests finishing a game or a full round there rather than just walking in. Head to that alley, start a game of bowling and play it through. It counts as one of the activity types for the Master of None trophy too, so try it early.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — a partnership with mass appeal — which suggests a moment where the partnership itself is the point, most likely something the two leads do together that draws a crowd. Play the story and the partner activities, and watch for a moment built around the pair being seen together. No exact step is claimed here, because the official description does not spell one out.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — PlayStation tracks a count up to 500, so this is the long cumulative trophy of the list. Choices appear throughout the story and side content: dialogue picks, decisions in missions, and forks in stranger strands. Say yes to choices when they appear rather than skipping past them, and play through the side content, since that is where most of the count lives. Because choices are spread across the whole game, this one is flagged missable in this guide only in the sense that you should not rush past decision moments — the count itself builds up over a full playthrough.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Succeed on your second try at something — the description is a riddle, and the honest reading is that this pops when you fail an attempt and then succeed on the very next one. That makes it the clearest missable in the list: it is about a specific retry, not a grind. The practical approach is to keep playing normally and let it come naturally when a retry succeeds; if you want to chase it, pick a repeatable challenge, fail it once on purpose, then pass it immediately after. Either way, it is a second-try moment, so it cannot be farmed by succeeding first time.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the description is a reaction, not an instruction, which points to a random or hidden event somewhere in Leonida. These moments usually happen while exploring off the beaten path, so keep exploring the odd corners of the map: the countryside, the swamps, the quiet beaches. No location is pinned down here, because none was verified in-game for this guide — treat it as an exploration trophy and let it surprise you.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — attack with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle and bowl the target over. Get a vehicle, pick up speed, and swing as you pass. It takes timing more than force: line the pass up, strike at the last moment, and keep driving. A quiet road with a pedestrian is the safest place to practise; wanted attention is the main risk, so pick your spot.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, and your contacts turn that dirty money clean — the game tracks how much you have laundered in total. Keep robbing, keep laundering what you earn through contacts as you go, and the quarter-million total builds up across the game. Do not sit on a pile of Marked Bills; launder regularly so the count keeps moving.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. This is cumulative spending, not one big purchase: clothes, weapons, vehicles, food and everything else you buy all counts. You will spend a large part of this naturally over a full playthrough, especially on vehicles and gear. If you are short near the end, buy the big-ticket items you still want — garage properties and vehicles — rather than wasting money on things you do not need.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are bought with in-game money, so this trophy is really a savings goal: keep earning through missions, robberies and laundering, and buy each garage property as you can afford it. Check the property list to see which ones you still own, and remember that spending here also counts toward the $100,000 shopping trophy — the two work together.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Find vehicles you have not registered yet — variety helps, since the app tracks distinct registrations — and register each one through the app. This pairs with discovering 100 vehicles: every new vehicle you find is a candidate for the app, so register as you discover rather than saving them all for the end.
trophies.name: On the Spot
